claim: The niri msg CLI has no --socket flag or socket-path option — every subcommand (Outputs, Workspaces, Windows, Action, EventStream, etc.) depends on the NIRI_SOCKET environment variable, so an external service wanting to use niri msg must inject NIRI_SOCKET explicitly or speak the JSON protocol over the socket file directly.
stance_target: gap-06: practical mechanism for an out-of-session service to drive niri IPC
quoted_support: pub enum Sub { /// Communicate with the running niri instance. Msg { #[command(subcommand)] msg: Msg, /// Format output as JSON. #[arg(short, long)] json: bool, }, ... } — no socket option anywhere in the CLI definition
